transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “So the living one reaches my father’s gate and thinks his purpose matters. Before you say his name, tell me what your mother put in the bread when the heat was worst. What fat, what grain, and how the smell changed when it touched the fire—say it exactly.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: She used coarse wheat and heavy ghee from our black goats.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Coarse wheat cuts the tongue if it is rushed. Did she sift it once or leave the stones in, and did the ghee smell sweet or sharp before it melted. Say what she added when your father was not watching.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: She sifted it twice and hid honey in the layers.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Twice means patience, not kindness. How much honey did she dare to hide—thin as breath or enough to drip when torn, and where did she keep it so the ants would not find it. Tell me what the kitchen smelled like just before the bread touched the fire.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It smelled like raw dough and dry wood smoke.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Dry smoke means the wood was old; raw dough means she waited too long. What spice did she keep wrapped in cloth for days like that, and did she grind it fresh or steal it already broken. Continue—what sound did the bread make when it first met the stone.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: She ground fresh fennel and it hissed against the clay.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Fennel is chosen, not found. Did she bruise the seeds with stone or tooth, and did the sweetness rise before the smoke or after. Say more—did Omar wait nearby when it hissed, or did he pretend not to care.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He sat close to steal the burnt edges.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Burnt edges are claimed, not given. Did your mother scold him with her mouth or only with her eyes, and did she tear the edge free or let him pull it himself. What did she brush on the torn place after—ghee again, or nothing at all.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: She swatted his hand and added sesame oil.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Sesame oil lingers longer than ghee; it clings. Was it pale or dark, and did the smell turn bitter at the edge or stay round and warm. Tell me what vessel she kept it in and where it sat in the kitchen.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It was dark oil kept in a heavy green bottle.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Green glass hides age; heavy means she trusted it. Did the bottle mouth chip where it met the stone, and did she wipe it with cloth or with her fingers after pouring. Say more—what else was on the shelf beside it, close enough to borrow its smell.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: A sack of dried black limes sat next to it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Black limes teach patience; they wait to be remembered. Were they split open or whole in the sack, and did their sour rise into the oil or stay trapped in the rind. When she reached past them, did her fingers come back dusty or clean.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Her fingers came back covered in gray dust.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Gray dust marks the faithful. Did she tap her fingers together over the floor or wipe them on her skirt, and did the dust leave ghosts in the air when she moved. Continue—what pot was already warming when her hands were gray.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The dented metal pot bubbled with lamb broth.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Lamb broth speaks of hours, not hunger. Was the fat clear on top or broken into white eyes, and did she skim it away or leave it to teach patience. Tell me what she dropped in first when it bubbled too hard—water, salt, or a quiet word.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: She threw in a handful of coarse salt.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Coarse salt cuts the noise. From where did she take it—an open bowl or a wrapped bundle—and did the grains stick to her skin when the steam rose. Say more, Salim: did Omar complain it was too much, or did he always say that only later.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He complained about the salt after finishing the bowl.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “After finishing means he wanted the world to bend around his full belly. When someone was sick, what did she make instead—broth thinned further, bread soaked soft, or something bitter she insisted would help. And at night, when the house slept, what did the kitchen smell like then.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: She soaked hard bread in warm milk and honey.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Milk and honey soften even pride. Was the milk goat or sheep, and did she warm it until skin formed or keep it thin and trembling. At night, after Omar slept, what lingered in the kitchen air—smoke, sweetness, or the clean dull smell of scrubbed metal.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It smelled of cold woodsmoke and old cardamom.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Cold smoke stays when the fire is remembered. Cardamom goes quiet before it fades; was it crushed fresh or kept whole in a jar she opened only then. Continue—what did Omar always ask for that she pretended to refuse before giving it anyway.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He wanted the marrow from inside the cracked leg bones.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text:
“Marrow. I hear that.”  
“Who cracked the bones—her hand or his, and did the sound snap clean or grind first. Did she salt the marrow or let it stay sweet, and where did he eat it when she finally gave it.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: She cracked them with the heavy stone pestle.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Stone does not hurry. Did she strike once or twice, and did the marrow slide out whole or smear against the bowl. Say exactly where Omar stood when he waited—by the door, the mat, or close enough to feel the heat.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He crouched right by the fire to watch it open.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: “Crouched means he trusted it would come to him. Did the fire pop when the bone opened, and did the marrow shine dull or bright in the flame. Tell me what she said to make him move back, and whether he listened the first time.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: She told him to move back, but he stayed close.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text:
“…Of course he did.”  
“When he stayed, did she laugh or go sharp, and what word did she use—his name or a threat she never meant. Tell me this last thing: did the marrow drip onto the coals, and what did the smoke smell like when it did.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It hissed on the coals and smelled like burnt fat.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text:
“Burnt fat is honest; it does not pretend to be anything else.”  
“You may go through.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is he behind the gate?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text:
“Behind is a simple word. He is where marrow finishes melting and the fire is no longer watched.”  
“Go.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I will look for the smoke.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text:
“Then follow it; smoke remembers its first warmth longer than names.”  
“Do not hurry—some doors open wider when you walk as if you already belong.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I will walk slow, like I live here.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text:
“Yes.”  
“The gate knows that walk.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am walking through to find him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text:
“Go, then.”  
“The heat you feel is not the fire; it is what stayed when someone watched it with you.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It feels like the air near the stove.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text:
“Keep that breath; it is the one thing this place does not spoil.”  
“Walk.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I will bring him back before the meat gets cold.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text:
“Before it gets cold,”  
“Yes.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He likes the marrow best.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text:
“I know.”  
“The gate is open.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He hates it when the fat hardens.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text:
“Yes.”  
“When it hardens, it means no one turned it with their fingers, no one breathed on it and laughed at the burn.”  
“Go.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: She burns the onions just how he likes.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text:
“Yes.”  
“That smell stays even when everything else forgets.”  
“Go.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: She hides the best meat under his rice.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text:
“So she hides it where hands will search without asking.”  
“I will not keep that from you.”  
“Go.”

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: She saves the burnt rice at the bottom for him.
